Resource: FHIR Version: R4B (4.3.0) — base resources: Device (vehicle) + Location (real-time position) + PractitionerRole (crew). NEW PROFILE — identified as a gap from real handover data (ambulances[] array with zero prior modeling).

Description: The unit's registration number, used as its primary identifier. Maps to ambulances[].id / registration_number.
Ambulance capability class. Maps to ambulances[].type (e.g. BLS, ALS).
Comments: REQUIRED (Min 1..1) AND MUST SUPPORT. Proposed values: BLS (Basic Life Support) | ALS (Advanced Life Support) | Air | Other.

Description: Ownership category, e.g. government, private, NGO. Maps to ownership_type.
Onboard telematics/tracking device identifier, if present. Maps to fleet_details.device.
Comments: OPTIONAL — not must-support; often blank in practice as seen in the sample payload.

Description: Phone number for the unit. Maps to phone_number.
Whether this unit has been stood down/replaced by another during the incident. Maps to relieved.
Comments: MUST SUPPORT (Min 0..1) — matters for MCI reporting where units are reassigned mid-incident; without this flag, a stood-down unit could be mistaken for one still actively responding.

Description: The unit's driver. Maps to assigned_driver.
The clinician aboard, distinct from the driver. Maps to assigned_practitioner.
Comments: MUST SUPPORT (Min 0..1) — this is typically the individual who should show up as Encounter.participant / Observation.performer / Procedure.performer on EMPOCEncounter; keep the reference consistent across all of them rather than re-identifying the same person differently per resource.

Description: The unit's current geographic position. Maps to ambulances[].latitude/longitude.
When the position was last refreshed. Maps to last_location_updated_at.
Comments: MUST SUPPORT (Min 0..1) — critical for knowing whether a displayed position is current or stale; a dispatch dashboard should visibly flag units whose last-updated timestamp is old.

Description: The unit's current response state, e.g. dispatched, en-route, on-scene, transporting, at-facility. Maps to response_status.
Comments: MUST SUPPORT (Min 0..1) — was empty in the sample payload but the field clearly exists in the source schema; populate whenever the dispatch system tracks it, since this drives real-time dispatch-board logic.
